svg.title: B-TREES AND B+ TREES: sketchnote
svg.text: Page-sized nodes full of keys: a few disk reads find any key among billions.
Each page holds boundary keys; follow the range that contains
your key. Branching factor ~500 → 3–4 levels for billions of
B+ trees keep values only in linked leaves: more keys per
internal page, shallower tree, cheap range scans. Databases
parent full too? it splits; a root split adds a level
Full leaf → two half-full pages + a new boundary key in the
parent. Only a root split adds a level. Every change goes
Descend once, then walk the linked leaves. Results come out
sorted, so ORDER BY and LIMIT are free.
Random UUIDv4 keys scatter inserts and
Writes are random page overwrites: LSM-trees
InnoDB: rows live in the primary-key B+ tree
"Postgres indexes are B+ trees: about three page
reads per lookup, and the date-range query is one
index range scan along the linked leaves. I'd use
time-ordered IDs so inserts append instead of
